entries.proposition: The protocol states the design: an RCT whose first period is the primary analysis, continued as an aggregated N-of-1 trial, with the N-of-1 analysis as the back-up if recruitment falls short.
entries.snippet: The outcome of the RCT design is the primary design for evaluation, with the aggregated N-of-1 design as a backup in case the inclusion numbers are not met for the RCT design.

entries.proposition: The authors state that an N-of-1 design applies only to chronic non-curable conditions where treatment must continue to suppress the symptom.
entries.snippet: N-of-1 trial methodology is limited to chronic non-curable diseases/symptoms and their treatments (treatment must be continued over time to supress the symptom or the disease).

entries.proposition: The stated advantage of the individual-control design is a smaller sample, half or less depending on evaluation cycles.
entries.snippet: Because treatment and placebo are evaluated in a single patient, a study needs far less patients (half or even less depending on evaluation cycles) for adequate power.

entries.proposition: Each patient receives three 6-week blinded periods with the intervention to placebo ratio 2 to 1, separated by 4-week wash-outs.
entries.snippet: The ratio of intervention to placebo periods is 2:1. In between treatments there are wash-out periods for 4 weeks.

entries.proposition: The primary outcome is the maximum bladder pain over the last 3 days on a 0 to 10 visual analogue scale.
entries.snippet: The primary objective is the maximum VAS bladder pain score in the last 3 days on a scale of 0–10.

entries.proposition: Efficacy is defined as success on any one of three criteria: 2 points on pain, 2 points on the most dominant symptom, or at least 5 on a 7-point global response scale.
entries.snippet: efficacy of GAG therapy for BPS/IC with Hunner lesions is defined by three possibilities: (1) an improvement of 2 points on the VAS pain score, or (2) an improvement of 2 points on the VAS score on the most dominant symptom that is reported by individual patient, or (3) an improvement of ≥5 on a 7-point GRA scale.

entries.proposition: The 2-point threshold was set by an interview with a patient panel, not by an anchor-based or distribution-based estimate.
entries.snippet: The improvement of 2 points on the VAS pain score and the most dominant symptom was established by an interview with a patient panel, to consider the heterogeneous symptoms in patient with BPS/IC.

entries.proposition: Aggregated analysis uses hierarchical Bayesian modelling and includes every patient who completed at least one treatment and one placebo period.
entries.snippet: All patients who completed at least one treatment and one placebo period will be included within the aggregated analysis, with inclusion of all available data.

entries.proposition: Power: 58 patients for the parallel comparison (80 with drop-out) against 28 (38 with drop-out) for the aggregated N-of-1 analysis; the effect size comes from an unblinded comparison with another instillation and the placebo effect from a different trial.
entries.snippet: Cervigni et al used the same HA-CS instillation that is used in this study and showed a treatment effect of approximately −4 on a VAS pain scale (0–10) in comparison with unblinded Dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO) instillations.

entries.proposition: The sample size for the aggregated design is computed to reach 80 percent power at 28 patients, 38 after drop-out.
entries.snippet: For the aggregated-N-of-1 trial design, >80% power will be achieved at 28 patients, considering the drop-out numbers, the required sample size was calculated at a total of 38 patients.

entries.proposition: The authors state that no earlier trial compared an aggregated N-of-1 design directly with a traditional RCT, which is the stated purpose of this study.
entries.snippet: So far, no aggregated N-of-1 trial has been directly compared with a traditional RCT.

entries.proposition: Both analyses use the same patients and the first period of the N-of-1 design is the RCT, so the two designs are nested, not independent replications.
entries.snippet: The GETSBI study is a double-blind multidesign multicentre randomised placebo-controlled trial

entries.proposition: Fig 1: Group A (n=40) receives placebo, then intervention, then intervention; Group B.1 (n=20) intervention, placebo, intervention; Group B.2 (n=20) intervention, intervention, placebo; each period has a 2-week run-in and run-out and 4-week wash-outs; the first period is labelled the standard RCT.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1 flow chart: Gr A n=40 run-in 2w, placebo 6w 1d/wk, wash-out 4w, intervention 6w, wash-out 4w, intervention 6w, run-out 2w; Gr B.1 n=20 intervention, placebo, intervention; Gr B.2 n=20 intervention, intervention, placebo; brackets mark Standard RCT over the first period, Single cross-over RCT over two, Multi cross-over design over all three.

entries.proposition: Fig 2: randomisation after eight exclusion criteria into Group A (40) and Group B (40), the latter split into two groups of 20; all 80 then enter an open phase of monthly instillations for 6 months.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2 flowchart: inclusion box adult patients with Hunner lesions and VAS 4 or more; eight exclusion criteria; randomisation; Group A n=40 placebo, intervention, intervention; Group B n=40 split B.1 n=20 and B.2 n=20; Fase II n=80 monthly instillations for 6 months.

entries.proposition: The comparison of designs will be made on significance level and on correlation of outcomes, as average changes with standard deviation.
entries.snippet: The study models will be compared on efficacy (significance) level and on correlation level.

entries.proposition: The sponsor frames the trial as evidence for a reimbursement decision, linking the design choice to a regulator-like requirement for objective measurements.
entries.snippet: as a requirement of the Dutch government for objective measurements
